stories.headline: Trump administration rejects UK plea for carve-out from Anthropic Fable/Mythos export ban

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration ruled out granting allied nations access to Anthropic's most advanced AI models, telling officials a G7 exemption would be 'completely illogical'
key_facts.excerpt: Amid the ongoing G7 summit, the Trump administration has reportedly ruled out granting allied nations access to Anthropic's most advanced AI models, maintaining restrictions imposed last week over national security concerns... granting exemptions to any G7 ally would be 'completely illogical.'

key_facts.fact: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer requested a carve-out so British nationals and companies could regain access to Mythos 5 and Fable 5; a senior White House official told the New York Post 'We can't have frontier models running amok'
key_facts.excerpt: Keir Starmer requested a carveout from the embargo on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models for British nationals and companies - and was denied. A senior White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told the New York Post: 'We can't have frontier models running amok'.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has suspended Fable 5 and Mythos 5 globally to comply with the US Commerce Department export controls served on Friday
key_facts.excerpt: The export order, served on Friday by the US Commerce Department, forced Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for every user worldwide to stay compliant.

key_facts.fact: US officials raised concerns that Anthropic's Fable 5 could be 'jailbroken' to unlock the more powerful cyber-security capabilities of Mythos 5; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick joined parts of the Anthropic talks remotely from the G7 summit
key_facts.excerpt: The restrictions were introduced after US officials raised concerns that Anthropic's recently released Fable 5 model could potentially be 'jailbroken', allowing users to unlock the more powerful cyber-security capabilities of Mythos 5. US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly joined parts of the talks remotely from the G7 summit in France

key_facts.fact: Insiders expect Trump will ultimately roll back the restriction globally rather than grant the UK a bespoke exemption; Anthropic and the administration continue direct negotiations
key_facts.excerpt: Insiders expect Trump will ultimately strike a deal that rolls back the restriction for everyone rather than grant Britain a bespoke exemption.

stories.headline: Apple targets late-2027 launch for camera AirPods, iPhone 20 Pro and 2nm A21 chips

key_facts.fact: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods, code-named B798, are scheduled to launch in late 2027, slipping from an original 2026 target due to AI software delays — they are Apple's first AI-focused wearable
key_facts.excerpt: Apple Inc.'s upcoming camera-equipped AirPods, a product meant to vault the company into the AI device market, is scheduled to launch in late 2027 as part of a flurry of new releases... The AirPods, code-named B798, were originally slated for release in 2026, according to the people. The deadline slipped in part because of Apple's prolonged struggles with artificial intelligence software.

key_facts.fact: AirPods cameras are not designed to capture photos or video — they act as sensors that feed visual context to Siri, with onboard lights indicating when data is being sent to the cloud
key_facts.excerpt: The cameras in the AirPods are not designed for taking photos and videos, and will instead send information about the wearer's surroundings to Siri. Siri will be able to answer questions about objects and whatever the wearer is looking at.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the AirPods, Apple plans to release a 20th-anniversary iPhone 20 Pro (V73) and iPhone 20 Max (V74) plus a second-generation foldable iPhone (V78), all powered by a 2-nanometer A21 chip internally codenamed Naxos

key_facts.fact: This year's iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and first-generation foldable will use the A20 Pro processor codenamed Borneo, while next year's base iPhone 18 will run the A20 Banda; Apple is also preparing an A22 Pro for 2028 that may be built on a 1.4-nanometer process
key_facts.excerpt: This year's iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and first-generation foldable iPhone will use an A20 Pro processor code-named Borneo. The standard iPhone 18 model arriving next year will run on a base A20 chip known internally as Banda.

key_facts.fact: The quick foldable follow-up — just a year after the first model — signals Apple is treating foldables as an annual product category

stories.headline: Binance set to lose EU access as Greek regulator poised to reject MiCA license bid

key_facts.fact: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, is set to lose permission to offer services to EU clients within weeks as its license application is about to be rejected, sources told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, is set to lose permission to serve European Union clients from next month because its licence application is about to be rejected, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Under MiCA rules, crypto firms have until the end of June 2026 to obtain a license; without it, Binance would not qualify to operate in the EU from July 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Under new EU rules, called MiCA, crypto firms have until the end of June to obtain a licence to allow them to keep servicing clients across the bloc. Binance's application, made to Greece's market regulator, is set to be turned down, the people said.

key_facts.fact: Binance has 300 million customers worldwide and has pursued the MiCA license for 18 months; the application was made through Greece's Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC).
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for Binance, which has 300 million customers worldwide, earlier said it has been pursuing a MiCA licence and had worked with regulators for 18 months.

key_facts.fact: Binance disputed the report, saying its understanding is that the HCMC considered its application compliant with MiCA requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our understanding is that the HCMC completed its review of the application and considered it compliant with MiCA requirements, and that the application was also reviewed at ESMA level,' a Binance spokesman told CoinDesk via email.

key_facts.fact: Co-CEO Richard Teng had said in February that Greece's labour force and security profile gave it the edge over larger financial centres as Binance's regulatory home in Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in February that Greece's labour force and security profile gave it the edge over larger financial centres for its regulatory home in Europe.

stories.headline: Brent crude closes below $80 for first time since March on Hormuz reopening hopes

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures fell 5% to close at $78.96 per barrel on Tuesday, the first time the international benchmark has settled below $80 since March.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures fell 5% to close at $78.96 per barrel, the first time the international benchmark has fallen below $80 since March. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures lost 5.8% to settle at $76.05.

key_facts.fact: WTI crude has plunged nearly 20% since the beginning of June, underlining the Strait of Hormuz's importance.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. benchmark, West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, fell 4% to $77.43 a barrel. WTI crude has plunged by nearly 20% since the beginning of June, underlining the Strait of Hormuz's continued importance to the oil market.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on arrival at G7 that the Strait of Hormuz will 'completely reopen' on Friday, free of Iranian tolls, after a signing ceremony in Geneva.
key_facts.excerpt: Arriving at the G7 meeting, President Donald Trump said the peace framework with Iran has been signed, adding that the Strait of Hormuz will 'completely reopen' on Friday, free of Iranian tolls. Trump said a formal signing ceremony would take place on Friday in Geneva.

key_facts.fact: BBC Verify's analysis of MarineTraffic data found just seven vessels appear to have passed through the strait since the deal was announced, while as many as 580 ships were waiting in the Gulf.
key_facts.excerpt: BBC Verify analysis of MarineTraffic ship-tracking data, however, shows that just seven vessels appear to have passed through the critical waterway since the deal was announced and as many as 580 ships appear to be waiting in the Gulf.

key_facts.fact: Mitsui OSK Lines CEO Jotaro Tamura said many tanker operators could wait weeks before allowing their tankers to resume transit through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Jotaro Tamura, chief executive of Mitsui OSK Lines, told the Financial Times on Tuesday that many operators could wait weeks until they allow their tankers to resume transit through the strait.

stories.headline: Sensor Tower: ChatGPT's global AI assistant share falls below 50% for first time

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT's global market share fell to 46.4% by end of May after Gemini rose to 27.7% and Claude to 10.3%; Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek and Meta AI each have under 5%
key_facts.excerpt: Until January, ChatGPT commanded over 50% market share, but by May's end, it had fallen to 46.4% thanks to the rise of Gemini (27.7%) and Claude (10.3%). Other assistants, including Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and Meta AI, have less than 5% market share.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT became the fastest mobile app ever to reach 1 billion monthly active users in May 2026, hitting the milestone in three years, faster than TikTok, YouTube, or Instagram
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT continues to lead the AI Assistant market, becoming the fastest mobile app ever to reach one billion monthly active users in May 2026. The app achieved the milestone in just three years—faster than TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT has 1.1B+ monthly users, followed by Gemini with 662M and Claude with 245M
key_facts.excerpt: The chatbot still remains the most popular AI assistant worldwide with over 1.1 billion monthly users, followed by Gemini with 662 million and Claude with 245 million.

key_facts.fact: Claude's True Audience was up 452% YoY in May and its US market share rose from 4.4% to nearly 14% over the same period
key_facts.excerpt: Claude has emerged as the fastest-growing challenger in 2026, with True Audience up 452% YoY in May and US market share rising from 4.4% to nearly 14% over the same period.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's deal with the US Department of War triggered a spike in ChatGPT uninstalls of ~200% above the app's average during the week of March 9-15; Claude logged more daily downloads than ChatGPT from March 1-5
key_facts.excerpt: In the United States, ChatGPT uninstalls surged following OpenAI's agreement with the Department of War, peaking at roughly 200% above the app's average during the week of March 9-15. Many users who uninstalled ChatGPT appeared to switch to Claude, following Anthropic's decision to decline a partnership with the Pentagon. Claude recorded more daily downloads than ChatGPT from March 1-5.

key_facts.fact: Global time spent on generative AI apps is projected to more than double YoY in H1 2026, from 17.2B hours in H1 2025 to 36B hours

stories.headline: G7 Evian summit issues joint statement backing US-Iran deal, pledges Strait of Hormuz mine-clearing mission

key_facts.fact: G7 leaders meeting at Evian adopted joint statements on the US-Iran peace deal and on geopolitical issues, plus declarations on migrant smuggling, drug trafficking, partnerships and calls on Ebola response and cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: At the 2026 G7 Leaders' Summit held in Evian, the leaders of the G7 discussed topics ranging from international peace and security to global economic stability, growth, and emerging technologies. They adopted the following statements: Leaders' declaration on mutually beneficial international partnerships; Leaders' call for a coordinated response to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak; Leaders' call on the fight against cancer; G7 Leaders' statement on geopolitical issues; Leaders' declaration on tackling migrant smugling; Leaders' declaration on the fight against drug trafficking.

key_facts.fact: UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada, Australia, EU and 9 other partners welcomed the MoU and committed to a 'strictly defensive and independent mission to reassure commercial shipping and conduct mine clearance operations' in the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The urgent re-opening of the Strait of Hormuz with unconditional and unrestricted freedom of navigation is essential. We are committed to playing our part to achieve this — in accordance with our respective constitutional requirements — including through a strictly defensive and independent mission to reassure commercial shipping and conduct mine clearance operations.

key_facts.fact: The statement said Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon and signatories are prepared to lift relevant sanctions in response to clear, verifiable steps by Iran on its nuclear program.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon. We stand ready to work with the US, Iran and the IAEA to this end. We are prepared to lift relevant sanctions in response to clear, verifiable steps by Iran on its nuclear programme.

key_facts.fact: Trump told fellow leaders in Evian: 'There's an agreement about one thing, that Iran will never have a [nuclear weapon], never, ever, ever. The rest of it's irrelevant, frankly.'
key_facts.excerpt: In Evian, US President Donald Trump assured fellow leaders that Tehran would not have a nuclear weapon. 'There's an agreement about one thing, that Iran will never have a [nuclear weapon], never, ever, ever. The rest of it's irrelevant, frankly,' Mr Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Arab leaders from UAE, Qatar and Egypt attended Tuesday's session; the summit also addresses Ukraine, with European leaders pressing Trump to rethink his Ukraine strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: European leaders will warn U.S. President Donald Trump at Tuesday's G7 summit that a superficial interim Iran deal risks entrenching Tehran's nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, while also pressing him to rethink his Ukraine strategy.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches Surface Pro 12 and Laptop 8 on Snapdragon X2, $500-$600 price hike

key_facts.fact: Microsoft launched the Surface Pro 12 (13-inch) starting at $1,499 and the Surface Laptop 8 (13.8-inch and 15-inch) starting at $1,599, both powered by Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 chips, available June 16, with Surface for Business versions following on July 14
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing the next Surface Pro and Surface Laptop, powered by Snapdragon X2 processors. The next Surface Pro and Surface Laptop ship with Snapdragon X2 processors... These new PCs are available starting June 16, with Surface for Business availability beginning July 14.

key_facts.fact: Starting prices are $500 higher for the Pro (was $999) and $600 higher for the Laptop (was $999) versus 2024 models, with Engadget attributing the increase to RAM and storage price spikes driven by AI investment
key_facts.excerpt: The new 13-inch Surface Pro starts at $1,499 (a $500 increase) while the updated Surface Pro 13.8-inch is a whopping $600 more expensive at $1,599. But I suppose Microsoft only has itself to blame, as its investments in AI are the biggest reason RAM and storage prices have skyrocketed lately.

key_facts.fact: Configurations use the 10-core Snapdragon X2 Plus or 12-core X2 Elite chips, skipping the 18-core X2 Elite and X2 Elite Extreme variants Qualcomm launched last year
key_facts.excerpt: The new 13.8-inch and 15-inch Laptops will include the Snapdragon X2 Plus 10-core chip, as well as the Snapdragon X2 Elite 12-core processor, passing over the 18-core X2 Elite and the 18-core X2 Elite Extreme that Qualcomm launched last year.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft claims up to 53% faster graphics on the Surface Pro and up to 58% faster on the Surface Laptop versus prior generation, with 15.5h battery life on the Pro and up to 20h on the 13.8-inch Laptop
key_facts.excerpt: Starting at $1,499 (MSRP), the new Surface Pro 13-inch with Snapdragon X2 delivers up to 53% faster graphic performance than the previous generation, up to 15.5 hours of battery life... Starting at $1,599 (MSRP), the Surface Laptop pairs the premium build quality Surface is known for with the power of Snapdragon X2 with up to 58% more graphics performance than the previous generation. The new Laptop delivers up to 20 hours of battery life on the 13.8-inch and up to 19 hours on the 15-inch.

key_facts.fact: Memory options span 16/24/32/64GB and storage options 256GB to 2TB on removable PCIe Gen 4 SSDs, with new Jade Surface Laptop and Dune Surface Pro Flex Keyboard color options

stories.headline: SpaceX exercises option to buy AI coding startup Cursor for $60B all-stock

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a binding agreement to acquire Anysphere (Cursor) in an all-stock deal valuing the company at $60 billion, expected to close in Q3 2026
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX has agreed to acquire AI coding startup Cursor in a $60 billion stock deal, just a few days after the space company's historic IPO... SpaceX said Tuesday that the acquisition is likely to close in the third quarter of this year.

key_facts.fact: The April option gave SpaceX the right to buy Cursor for $60B or pay a $10B break-up fee ($1.5B cash plus $8.5B in computing resources)
key_facts.excerpt: In April, SpaceX said it had obtained the right to acquire Cursor for $60 billion later this year. If, for some reason, the deal is not consummated, SpaceX had agreed to pay Cursor a 'termination fee' of $1.5 billion, and $8.5 billion in computing resources, according to its IPO filings.

key_facts.fact: The $60B in Class A common stock represented 3.4% dilution at SpaceX's IPO valuation
key_facts.excerpt: The $60 billion in class A common stack that SpaceX has agreed to pay to acquire Cursor represented a 3.4% dilution at the aerospace and tech conglomerate's IPO valuation.

key_facts.fact: Cursor was on track to close a $2B round from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Nvidia at a $50B valuation before SpaceX intervened
key_facts.excerpt: The company, founded in 2022 and led by 25-year-old chief executive Michael Truell, was on track to close a $2bn round from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Nvidia at a $50bn valuation before SpaceX intervened.

key_facts.fact: Deal structure: SpaceX subsidiary X67 Inc. merges into Cursor, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary; Cursor shares convert based on SpaceX's average share price over the seven trading days before close
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX subsidiary, X67 Inc., will merge into Cursor, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary. Cursor's shares convert into SpaceX Class A stock based on an implied equity value of $60bn, priced on the company's average share price over the seven trading days before the deal closes.

key_facts.fact: Acquisition is meant to help SpaceX's AI division (built around the xAI merger earlier this year) close the gap with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex
key_facts.excerpt: Musk has previously expressed his frustration with xAI's sub-par coding product, which lags behind popular tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. Acquiring Cursor, which offers similar tools to automate coding, could help close the gap.

stories.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.2: 1M-context coding model under MIT license, beats GPT-5.5

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup Z.ai (formerly Zhipu) released GLM-5.2, a 753B-parameter open-weights LLM with a stable 1M-token context window, under an unrestricted MIT license
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Chinese AI startup Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI) announced the immediate release of GLM-5.2, a 753-billion parameter open-weights large language model (LLM) engineered specifically to dominate 'long-horizon' autonomous coding and engineering tasks... z.ai has released GLM-5.2's core weights under an unrestricted MIT open-source license

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.2 trails Anthropic's Opus 4.8 by just 1% on FrontierSWE while outperforming GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on multiple coding benchmarks, ranking the highest open-source model on FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, and SWE-Marathon
key_facts.excerpt: Across FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, and SWE-Marathon, it consistently ranks among the top models overall—trailing Opus 4.8 by just 1% on FrontierSWE, outperforming GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 on multiple benchmarks, and remaining the highest-ranked open-source model across all three.

key_facts.fact: Architecture: mixture-of-experts with ~744-753B total parameters and roughly 40B active per token; the new IndexShare technique reuses one indexer across four sparse-attention layers, cutting per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at 1M context
key_facts.excerpt: Improved Architecture: We propose IndexShare, which reuses the same indexer across every four sparse attention layers, reducing per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at a 1M context length. We also improve GLM-5.2's MTP layer for speculative decoding, increasing the acceptance length by up to 20%

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens; enterprise subscriptions start at $12.60/month
key_facts.excerpt: Available immediately on Hugging Face, the Z.ai API, and more than 20 third-party coding environments, the model boasts a highly stable 1-million-token context window alongside enterprise subscription tiers starting at just $12.60 per month... GLM-5.2 API access is priced at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens

key_facts.fact: The 1M-token context is a 5x jump over GLM-5.1's 200K limit, putting GLM-5.2 among the rare open-weight models that can process book-length inputs in one pass
key_facts.excerpt: GLM-5.2's predecessor, GLM-5.1, topped out at 200,000 tokens. This new version handles five times that amount, putting it in rare company among open-weight models that can actually process book-length inputs in a single pass.
